title: A relatively flat module descends on a fixed affine-limit model
statement: Let $I$ be a directed partially ordered set, let $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ be a diagram of Noetherian rings, and let $S$ be an affine scheme with a limiting cone over the inverse system $\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Fix $i\in I$ and a finitely presented morphism $f_i:Z_i\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $Z=Z_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $M$ be a finitely presented module on $Z$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] flat over $S$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. There exist $j\ge i$ and a finitely presented module $M_j$ on $Z_j=Z_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}\operatorname{Spec}(R_j)$, flat over $\operatorname{Spec}(R_j)$, together with an isomorphism between its tensor pullback along the canonical comparison $Z\to Z_j$ and $M$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-base-change].

proof.text: Apply the object clause of finitePresentation_module_map_descent to M. Finite presentation supplies quasicoherence, and the result gives j >= i, a finitely presented quasicoherent module N on the fixed base-change model at j, and eN identifying its limit moduleBaseChange with M.

Transfer hM through eN using Scheme.Modules.IsFlatOver.of_iso, whose proof evaluates the sheaf isomorphism on affine opens and transports flatness under the induced linear equivalence. Compare the direct and iterated cartesian models via their unique isomorphism. For an isomorphism of schemes, restriction identifies the section modules on corresponding affine opens; appLE_comp_appLE identifies their base actions. Uniqueness of tensor-pullback left adjoints and tensorPullbackComp then transport flatness between the two models. These comparisons are proved as private helpers, with no assumed flatness lemma.

At starting index j and source pullback.snd fi (Spec.map R_ij), apply the finite affine chart comparison lemma to N and the transported limit flatness. For each of its finitely many chart modules use affine eventual flatness with the first algebra equal to R_j. Induct over Finset.univ to choose a common upper bound of j and all chart thresholds; the empty set uses j. At that stage the chart comparison glues flatness to the iterated pullback. The private eventual-flatness proof follows the existing FlatModuleDescent proof but imports only its acyclic chart and algebra dependencies.

Take Nk to be moduleBaseChange fi gk applied to N. Tensor pullback preserves its finite presentation. The proved cartesian comparison transfers iterated-pullback flatness to Nk. The cone equation and baseChangeMap_comp identify the composite comparison morphism with the original one; tensorPullbackCompositionIso gives the inverse comparison on N, and composing it with eN gives Nk pulled back to the limit isomorphic to M.

theorem exists_flat_module_on_later_stage
    {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [IsDirectedOrder I]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ k : I, IsNoetherianRing (R.obj k)]
    (c : Cone (R.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec)) (hc : IsLimit c) [IsAffine c.pt]
    (i : I) {Zi : Scheme.{u}} (fi : Zi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation fi] [QuasiCompact fi] [QuasiSeparated fi]
    (M : (pullback fi (c.π.app (Opposite.op i))).Modules) [M.IsFinitePresentation]
    (hM : M.IsFlatOver (pullback.snd fi (c.π.app (Opposite.op i)))) :
    ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j)
      (Mj : (pullback fi (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))).Modules),
      Mj.IsFinitePresentation ∧
      Mj.IsFlatOver (pullback.snd fi (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))) ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange fi
        (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
        (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (Opposite.op i)))
        (Over.homMk (c.π.app (Opposite.op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))).obj Mj ≅ M)
